taxonomy_notes: POWO accepts the species with three accepted subspecies. Source pool does not identify subspecies or cultivar. Avoid assigning either from an ornamental photo.
look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Opposite SIMPLE leaves with one blade deeply palmately divided into usually 5–7 pointed, finely toothed lobes; verify opposite buds and paired winged samaras. Cultivars vary widely in leaf shape and color; red foliage alone is not diagnostic.

project_inclusion.notes: Approved source-pool learner admission; native outside North America per POWO, not a target-county native PASS. Do not infer invasive status.
project_inclusion.source_pool: Master Plant Pool row 12; installer preflight mass-01
project_inclusion.range_basis: POWO: native Japan and Korea; no Texas-native PASS.

morphology_keys.habit: Deciduous small ornamental tree or shrub, highly variable by cultivar.
morphology_keys.leaves_attachment: Opposite, simple, palmately 5–7(–9)-lobed serrate leaves with deep sinuses; no separate leaflets.
morphology_keys.flower_reproductive: Small inconspicuous spring flowers; use opposite foliage and fruit for confirmation.
morphology_keys.fruit_seed: Paired winged samaras attached at the seed ends.
morphology_keys.stem_bud: Opposite twigs and buds; often smooth bark on young shoots.

confused_with: Acer grandidentatum: usually broader 3–5 lobes and shallower sinuses.
Acer saccharinum: deeper angular lobes and silvery lower leaf surface.
Acer negundo: compound leaves of separate leaflets.
Liquidambar styraciflua: alternate leaves and spiky spherical fruit.
comparisons.key_distinctions: Opposite simple deeply divided leaves plus paired samaras, not boxelder leaflets or sweetgum balls.
